what_it_does: Modern graphics processors (GPUs) contain several distinct types of arithmetic units: small general-purpose units for simple math (scalar), wider units that do the same operation across many numbers at once (vector), and specialized tensor-math units that multiply large grids of numbers in one shot (tensor cores). Existing software compilers that translate AI workloads into GPU instructions typically pick just one type of unit and use it exclusively, leaving the other types sitting idle. Mosaic is a compiler technique that instead carves a single computation into smaller sub-tasks, each matched to the most suitable unit type, and runs all three unit types simultaneously like parallel lanes on a highway. A compiler pass automatically figures out the best way to divide the work, then stitches together the mixed-instruction program that keeps all units busy at once, improving throughput without changing the underlying GPU chip.
